insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA for modeled attribution; this protocol settles verified purchase confirmation at roughly $0.10 per receipt — a 50–200x cost difference driven by the receipt itself serving as the conversion event, not a proxy for one.

With Chrome completing cookie deprecation and device fingerprinting increasingly blocked by privacy law and browser hardening, the industry has no cross-site deterministic signal at scale — verified email receipts are structurally positioned to fill that gap without identity attachment.

Amazon knows Amazon purchases; Walmart knows Walmart purchases; neither knows the other — and no brand does either. This protocol ingests email receipts regardless of platform participation, producing the only cross-ecosystem purchase dataset that doesn't require any retailer to open their silo.

With confirmed adoption across non-metro California, Idaho, Wisconsin, and Pennsylvania, the receipt dataset is reaching geographies that probabilistic ad tech systematically underserves due to its urban-panel bias — 16 active CBSAs growing through social graph diffusion, not paid acquisition.

Category entropy is holding at 3.131 bits with AAA marking the first service-sector brand entry alongside grocery, home improvement, and QSR — the basket is broadening, not concentrating, which increases the dataset's utility for cross-category attribution modeling.

insights.topic: Merchant resolution gap as premium spend undercount
insights.insight: 11% of receipts fail merchant name resolution, and the unclassified category carries the highest average basket value at $133.50 — meaning current brand-level analysis is likely undercounting high-value purchase signals, not overcounting them.
